evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.85, LEFT vertical double arrow (first of the three drawn equilibria of the left/bottom branch). Step 1 of 3: the C1-O4 bond of protonated methyl isopropyl ether stretches into the drawn ion-neutral complex 'CH2(H)-CH(CH3)...O(+)(H)CH3' (dashed C...O bond, the labile methyl H drawn out). That complex is non-covalent and is APPROXIMATED here by the fully separated pair isopropyl cation + methanol, because a partial bond has no RDKit bond order; nothing drawn on the page is silently dropped - the complex is disclosed here. Book draws 0 arc(s): Equation 8.85 contains NO curved electron-pushing arrows at all - it is drawn with straight reaction/equilibrium arrows plus dashed 'partial bond' strokes that denote the loose bonds of the ion-neutral complexes. The single encoded move <1> (the C1-O4 pair onto the oxygen) is reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page).

locator.panel: lower-left vertical double arrow (middle-left to bottom-left)

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.85, LOWER-LEFT vertical double arrow. Step 2 of 3: inside the ion-neutral complex the isopropyl cation isomerises to the n-propyl cation - the page redraws the complex at the bottom left as 'CH2(+)...O(H)CH3' over 'CH2' over 'CH3', i.e. the '+' has moved to a TERMINAL carbon and the oxygen is now drawn neutral. MECHANISM: 1,2-hydride shift, the H7-C2 sigma pair migrating to the carbenium centre C1 so that the charge lands on C2. The migrating hydrogen is the same [1H:7] atom that Equation 8.85b transfers to oxygen, which is why the page draws it explicitly in the middle-left structure. Methanol is carried through as a spectator so the complex is represented at both ends of the step. Book draws 0 arc(s): Equation 8.85 contains NO curved electron-pushing arrows at all - it is drawn with straight reaction/equilibrium arrows plus dashed 'partial bond' strokes that denote the loose bonds of the ion-neutral complexes. The encoded move <1> is reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page).

Equation 8.85, BOTTOM horizontal double arrow. Step 3 of 3: the n-propyl-cation / methanol complex collapses to the covalent oxonium ion drawn at the bottom right, protonated methyl n-propyl ether CH3CH2CH2-O(+)(H)-CH3 (the page draws the C-O bond solid here and the '+' back on the oxygen). MECHANISM: an oxygen lone pair forms the new O4-C2 bond. NET EFFECT of steps 1-3: the drawn skeletal isomerisation of protonated methyl ISOPROPYL ether into protonated methyl n-PROPYL ether, both C4H11O+ at m/z 75.0804, which is how the page shows that C-H bonds of either propyl isomer become available for the proton transfer of Equation 8.85b. Book draws 0 arc(s): Equation 8.85 contains NO curved electron-pushing arrows at all - it is drawn with straight reaction/equilibrium arrows plus dashed 'partial bond' strokes that denote the loose bonds of the ion-neutral complexes. The encoded move <1> is reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page). CONTEXT: the p.199 text introduces Equation 8.85 with 'In the absence of activating functional groups in EE ions, proton-exchange reactions can proceed in ion-molecule complexes (Equations 8.14, 8.85; Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991); demonstration of such pathways usually requires D-labeling. Here both the hydrogen lability and site receptivity' [continues on p.200] 'are determined by the relative proton affinities of the donor and acceptor sites: PA(C3H6, CH3OH) = 7.8, 7.9 eV. Note that the competitive dissociations of such a proton-bound isomer of (AB + H)+ produce AH+ and BH+, whose mass sum equals AB + 2.' The reacting ion is therefore the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether, C4H11O+, curator-computed monoisotopic m/z 75.0804; the page prints no m/z for it. The two percentages printed on the page (40%, 60%) are the BRANCHING abundances of the two competing dissociation channels, not 70 eV EI relative intensities.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.85, so no MØD rule is cross-linked. Candidates checked and REJECTED: IMS_8_10 ('[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)>>...[C+]5....[O]8{=}[C]9...') and IMS_8_12 both require an OXOCARBENIUM precursor - the left side pins a DOUBLE bond [O+]8{=}[C]9 - whereas Equation 8.85 starts from a protonated ether whose O+ carries three single bonds (C, H, CH3); the pattern cannot match this substrate even though the bond that breaks (C-O, heterolytic, charge retained on carbon) is of the same inductive type. IMS_8_14_1/_1b (the proton-bound-complex rH pair) are additionally atom-unbalanced (their product half carries an extra methyl copy-pasted from IMS_8_13). The IMS_8_7_* 'hydrogen exchange in an ion-molecule complex' family operates on odd-electron ketone/enol systems, not on a protonated ether. Equation 8.85 is unmodelled by the current rule set.

ms_context.activation_method: unspecified - the page names no ionization or activation experiment; the reacting ion is the protonated molecule (AB+H)+ of methyl isopropyl ether discussed in the p.199/200 text (Terlouw et al. 1986; Bowen 1991). ionization_method 'CI' is the curator's inference for how an (AB+H)+ ion is made, NOT a statement printed on the page
